NVIDIA is a semiconductor company founded in 1993, best known for the graphics processing units (GPUs) that power gaming, professional visualisation, and increasingly artificial intelligence. It trades on the NASDAQ under the ticker NVDA.

NVIDIA designs GPUs and the surrounding software ecosystem. Its chips accelerate workloads from real-time graphics to large-scale machine learning, and its CUDA software platform has become a de facto standard for general-purpose GPU computing. The company sells into gaming, data centres, professional visualisation, and automotive markets.

NVIDIA's long bet was that parallel computation on GPUs would matter far beyond graphics. That bet paid off as machine learning came to rely on the massive parallelism GPUs provide, making NVIDIA a central supplier of the hardware behind modern AI.

NVIDIA became one of the most valuable companies in the world on the back of demand for AI accelerators, joining the small group of US firms to cross multi-trillion-dollar valuations. Its data-centre business now rivals or exceeds its historical gaming roots, and its results are widely watched as a barometer for AI infrastructure spending.

# Microsoft: Full Picture

**Current Price:** MSFT is at $411.74 (-1.18% today), with volume of 22.9M shares.

## What Microsoft Does

Microsoft is a multinational technology company founded in 1975, one of the largest software and cloud-computing firms in the world. It trades on the NASDAQ under the ticker MSFT.

The company develops, licenses, and supports software, services, devices, and cloud infrastructure. Its best-known products include the Windows operating system, the Office and Microsoft 365 productivity suite, the Azure cloud platform, the Xbox gaming business, and the LinkedIn professional network. Azure and Microsoft 365 anchor a large, subscription-based enterprise business.

Microsoft's modern strategy centres on cloud and recurring software revenue—moving customers from one-off licences to subscriptions and consumption-based cloud services. Azure positions Microsoft as one of the dominant providers of cloud infrastructure, while deep enterprise relationships give it broad reach across business computing.

The company's 1986 IPO created one of the largest concentrations of wealth in technology. After a period of slower growth in the 2000s, a strategic pivot to cloud under new leadership returned it to the front rank of the industry. It is among the most heavily weighted constituents of the S&P 500 and a major influence on the technology sector.

## Recent News

Microsoft continues to strengthen its position in the AI and quantum computing sectors, unveiling the Majorana 2 quantum chip while maintaining strong growth in Azure's AI revenue. The company is experiencing a boost in analyst confidence with a raised price target amid a robust tech sector rally.

Billionaire investor Bill Ackman of Pershing Square has laid out one of the more provocative big-cap calls of this AI cycle, arguing that Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon could be comparable to adding Berkshire Hathaway 25 years ago.

OpenAI and Microsoft reached a deal to complete the startup's shift to for-profit, marking a significant development in their partnership.
